title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Measures for the Training, Assessment, Rewards, and Punishments of People's Jurors
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court  Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the Measures for the Training, Assessment, Rewards, and Penalties of People's Assessors

Fa Fa [2019] No. 12

The High People's Courts and Judicial Bureaus (Departments) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, and the Production and Construction Corps Judicial Bureau of Xinjiang:

In order to conscientiously implement the People's Assessors Law of the PRC and further standardize the training, assessment, rewards, and penalties of people's assessors, the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice have studied and formulated the Measures for the Training, Assessment, Rewards, and Penalties of People's Assessors, which are hereby issued to you for your careful implementation in light of actual circumstances.

If significant situations or problems arise during implementation in various localities, please promptly report them to the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice.

April 24, 2019

Measures for the Training, Assessment, Rewards, and Penalties of People's Assessors

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Assessors Law to standardize the training, assessment, rewards, and penalties of people's assessors.

Article 2 The daily management work of training, assessment, rewards, and penalties of people's assessors shall be undertaken by the basic people's court jointly with the judicial administrative organ. The people's court and the judicial administrative organ shall strengthen communication and contact and establish a coordination and cooperation mechanism.

Article 3 The people's court and the judicial administrative organ shall establish organs or designate specific persons to be responsible for the training, assessment, rewards, and penalties of people's assessors, with other relevant departments providing cooperation.

Article 4 Matters closely related to people's assessors' participation in trial activities, such as notification of court sessions, pre-trial review of files, investigation and inquiries, participation in mediation, arrangement of deliberations, and signature of documents, shall be the responsibility of each trial department. Other management matters, including random selection, coordination and liaison, distribution of allowances, and delivery of judgments, shall be the responsibility of the department determined by the people's court based on the actual circumstances of that court.

Article 5 The Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice shall improve supporting mechanisms, build technical platforms according to their respective responsibilities, develop a management system for people's assessors, strengthen system integration and information data sharing, and provide technical support for improving the information management, random selection, balanced participation in trials, performance information, performance evaluation, assessment training, and feedback of opinions of people's assessors.

Article 6 The basic people's court shall issue a People's Assessor Work Certificate to the people's assessor. The unified style of the People's Assessor Work Certificate shall be formulated and issued by the Political Department of the Supreme People's Court, and each court shall print it itself. After a people's assessor's term expires or they are removed from office in accordance with law, the people's court shall retrieve or cancel the People's Assessor Work Certificate held by that person.

Article 7 Except as provided by law, the people's court and the judicial administrative organ shall not disclose personal information such as the contact information and home address of the people's assessor.

Article 8 While performing trial duties in accordance with law, people's assessors shall comply with the Basic Code of Ethics for Judges of the PRC.

Chapter II Training

Article 9 Training for people's assessors is divided into pre-service training and in-service training. The people's court shall, jointly with the judicial administrative organ, conduct training for people's assessors in a planned and organized manner. The training shall meet the actual needs of people's assessors in participating in trial activities. Training content includes political theory, assessor duties, judges' professional ethics, trial discipline, and basic legal knowledge. Training content may also be arranged in light of the characteristics and types of cases in the local region.

Article 10 The education and training authorities and relevant business departments of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice shall be responsible for formulating unified training outlines and training materials for people's assessors, putting forward clear training and teaching requirements, and regularly supervising and inspecting the training work of people's assessors. When necessary, they may hold demonstration training classes for people's assessors and training classes for trainers of people's assessors.

Article 11 The education and training authorities and judge training institutions of the High People's Court shall be responsible for the training planning and related management and coordination work for people's assessors within their respective jurisdictions. When the education and training authorities and judge training institutions of the High People's Court undertake the task of pre-service training for people's assessors within their jurisdictions, they may use information technology methods such as remote video, and the basic people's court shall organize and cooperate jointly with the judicial administrative organ. The High People's Court shall, jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level, formulate an annual training plan and implementation opinions for the training work of people's assessors within its jurisdiction, and report them separately to the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice for record.

Article 12 In-service training shall mainly be undertaken by the basic people's court to which the people's assessor belongs jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level. The training and teaching plan shall be examined and approved by the intermediate people's court. For municipalities directly under the Central Government, the training and teaching plan shall be examined and approved by the High People's Court. When necessary, the education and training authorities and judge training institutions of qualified intermediate people's courts may be entrusted to undertake training tasks for people's assessors.

Article 13 The basic people's court shall, jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level, promptly submit the list of persons to receive pre-service training and training opinions to the education and training authorities of the higher people's court, the judge training institution, and the relevant business department of the judicial administrative organ.

Article 14 Training for people's assessors shall be conducted by combining centralized full-time training with on-the-job self-study. It may also be conducted by segmenting training and accumulating class hours based on actual circumstances. In addition to centralized lectures, training methods may include court observation, thematic seminars, case teaching, simulation demonstrations, audiovisual teaching, circuit teaching, and various other forms. The duration of pre-service training shall generally be no less than 40 class hours. The duration of in-service training shall be reasonably determined by the people's court based on actual circumstances and needs.

Article 15 The people's court and the judicial administrative organ shall provide venues, training facilities, and other necessary training conditions for people's assessors to participate in training.

Chapter III Assessment and Rewards

Article 16 The basic people's court, jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level, shall assess the performance of people's assessors in performing trial duties.

Article 17 The assessment of people's assessors shall combine regular assessment with annual assessment. Regular assessment shall be conducted by the basic people's court jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level, determining the assessment time and method based on actual circumstances. Annual assessment shall be conducted by the basic people's court jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level at the end of each year. In the annual assessment, the performance of people's assessors in performing their duties shall be rated as excellent, competent, basically competent, or incompetent.

Article 18 The basic people's court shall formulate assessment methods for people's assessors performing trial duties and shall solicit the opinions of the judicial administrative organ at the same level.

Article 19 The assessment content for people's assessors includes ideological and moral character, actual performance in assessor work, work attitude, trial discipline, trial conduct, and participation in training.

Article 20 Where an intermediate people's court or a High People's Court randomly selects people's assessors from the list of people's assessors of basic people's courts within its jurisdiction to participate in the trial work of that court, and where maritime courts, intellectual property courts, railway transport courts, and other courts that do not have a corresponding people's congress at the same level randomly select people's assessors from the list of people's assessors of basic people's courts within the jurisdiction of the prefecture-level city where they are located or within the case jurisdiction to participate in the trial of cases, those courts shall notify the basic people's court to which the people's assessor belongs of the performance of duties by the people's assessor in that court, which shall serve as one of the bases for the assessment of the people's assessor. The time and method for notifying the performance of duties shall be specifically coordinated by the aforementioned courts and the court to which the people's assessor belongs.

Article 21 The basic people's court shall promptly notify the people's assessor personally, the unit to which the assessor belongs, and the grassroots self-governing organization or people's organization at the place of household registration or habitual residence of the assessor in writing of the annual assessment results. If a people's assessor disagrees with the assessment results, they may apply for a review to the basic people's court where they serve within five days of receiving the written notice of the assessment results. The basic people's court shall make a review decision within fifteen days of receiving the review application and notify the people's assessor personally, the unit to which the assessor belongs, and the grassroots self-governing organization or people's organization at the place of household registration or habitual residence of the assessor in writing.

Article 22 The assessment results shall serve as the basis for commending and rewarding people's assessors.

Article 23 People's assessors who have made outstanding achievements or other notable deeds in trial work shall be commended and rewarded by the basic people's court jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level in accordance with relevant provisions. Commendations and rewards shall adhere to the principles of legality, fairness, openness, and impartiality.

Article 24 People's assessors who have any of the following performances may be deemed to have made outstanding achievements or other notable deeds in trial work: (1) Having proposed reform suggestions for trial work that are adopted and produce significant results; (2) Having proposed judicial suggestions for cases in which they participated that are adopted by relevant departments; (3) Having actively exerted subjective initiative in assessor work, maintaining social stability, with notable deeds; (4) Having other outstanding achievements or notable deeds.

Article 25 The basic people's court shall promptly notify the people's assessor personally, the unit to which the assessor belongs, and the grassroots self-governing organization or people's organization at the place of household registration or habitual residence of the assessor in writing of the decision on commendation and reward for the people's assessor.

Chapter IV Removal from Office and Disciplinary Sanctions

Article 26 After the term of a people's assessor expires, the office is automatically terminated. The basic people's court shall, jointly with the judicial administrative organ, make a public announcement on its official website or in local mainstream media. It is not necessary to submit a request to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level to remove the people's assessor's office. When a people's assessor's term expires, if a case in which they participated has not yet concluded, they may continue to perform trial duties until the date the case is concluded.

Article 27 If a people's assessor has one of the circumstances provided for in Article 27 of the People's Assessors Law, and after verification by the basic people's court where the person serves jointly with the judicial administrative organ, the president of the court shall submit a request to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level to remove the people's assessor's office.

Article 28 If a people's assessor is removed from office, the basic people's court shall notify the removed person personally, the unit to which the person belongs, and the grassroots self-governing organization or people's organization at the place of household registration or habitual residence of the person in writing, and simultaneously send a copy of the removal list to the judicial administrative organ at the same level. The basic people's court and the judicial administrative organ shall report the removal list step by step to the High People's Court and the provincial judicial administrative organ for record.

Article 29 If a people's assessor engages in conduct listed in Item (3) or (4) of Paragraph 1 of Article 27 of the People's Assessors Law, and after verification by the basic people's court where the person serves jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level, measures may be taken to impose disciplinary sanctions, including notifying the unit to which the person belongs, the grassroots self-governing organization or people's organization at the place of household registration or habitual residence, and making a public notice within the jurisdiction area.

Article 30 If a people's assessor engages in conduct listed in Item (4) of Paragraph 1 of Article 27 of the People's Assessors Law, the basic people's court where the person serves shall, jointly with the judicial administrative organ at the same level, conduct verification; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with law.

Chapter V Supplementary Provisions

Article 31 These Measures shall be jointly interpreted by the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice.

Article 32 These Measures shall take effect as of May 1, 2019. Where any provisions on the management of training, assessment, rewards, and penalties of people's assessors formulated by the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice before the effective date of these Measures are inconsistent with these Measures, these Measures shall prevail.
